column11: No progression-free survival exists for JSB462 with Pluvicto until NCT07047118 reads out, so this uses its control arm. In PSMAfore, taxane-naive PSMA-positive mCRPC after one ARPI, Pluvicto's median radiographic progression-free survival was 11.60 months at the third data cutoff, median follow-up 24.11 months (Morris et al., Lancet 2024;404:1227-39, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01653-2, PubMed abstract). JSB462 is taken daily until progression, so at a constant hazard 0.5^(12/11.60) = 48.82% remain after a year and 51.18% stop
column12: treat-to-progression, so the PFS route. The primary analysis gave 9.30 months, which would stop 59.1%. NCT07047118 admits men after up to two taxane regimens, who progress sooner than PSMAfore's taxane-naive patients, which argues for faster stopping

column11: judgement: no Phase 3 is registered (ClinicalTrials.gov search on JSB462, luxdegalutamide and ARV-766, 2026-09-28). Pluvicto, the last new medicine approved after an ARPI in this disease and this drug's partner, went from its Phase 3 start (VISION, NCT03511664, 2018-05-29) to approval (NDA215833, 2022-03-23, openFDA) and a first full year in 2023, about 4.6 years. column11: ANCHOR, a measured share of the line. JSB462's lead use is added to Pluvicto (NCT07047118), so the patients it can reach are the ones who take Pluvicto. Among US mCRPC patients who started first-line therapy in 2024 (Flatiron, about 280 mostly community centres), Lu-177 was 47 of 344 second-line starts, 13.7% (Hooper et al., JAMA Netw Open 2026;9(6):e2620750, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20750, PMC13316606), up from 18 of 894 (2.0%) in the 2021 cohort. Second line is the first line after an ARPI for most of the pool: 4,041 of 5,096 first lines (79.3%) across the 2021 to 2025 cohorts were an ARPI. So the base case gives JSB462 every Pluvicto patient in the line it is tested in. No independent peak forecast for JSB462 or ARV-766 was found: Novartis and Arvinas give none, and a search of analyst coverage found none
column12: The case for more: Pluvicto is also taken later, 23 of 89 third-line starts (25.8%) in the 2024 cohort, and across all lines of the 2021 to 2025 cohorts Lu-177 was started 723 times (113, 187, 215, 137 and 71 from first to fifth line) against about 2,600 men who reached a line after an ARPI (705 ARPI-experienced at first line, plus 3,541 ARPI-naive men started on an ARPI of whom the cohort's 53.6% reached a second line), roughly 28%; Pluvicto's pre-taxane label (efficacy supplement approved 2025-03-28, NDA215833) postdates most of that follow-up. The case for less: an add-on reaches only part of its partner's patients, the combination must beat Pluvicto alone (primary endpoint PSA50), Pluvicto's label now carries PSMA-positive hormone-sensitive disease in combination with an ARPI (efficacy supplement 37 approved 2026-07-31, NDA215833, openFDA; label effective 2026-08-12), which moves some of its use out of this line, and opevesostat, ifinatamab deruxtecan and JNJ-101556143 claim the same pool
